To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prospects for citizen involvement in urban governance in the neighbourhoods we examined are likely to be greatest in those areas that are more affluent and where the local population is better educated.

the prospects for citizen involvement in neighbourhood governance are enhanced in neighbourhoods where the local government is committed to citizen participation, where local institutions and organisations are more numerous and diverse, and where the residents are more educated, have greater social trust, and are more likely to be involved in community activities.

1) civic culture, as well as community and neighbourhood characteristics, are important in shaping citizen participation; 2) the relationship between civic culture and citizen participation is mediated by political institutions, public policy and the nature of local governance; and 3) political mobilization, the creation of opportunity structure, and the adoption of participatory approaches to local government are more important than the level of civic culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between civic culture, community and citizen participation in urban neighbourhoods.
the role of civic culture and community in shaping citizen participation.
the role of civic culture and citizen participation in the context of urban governance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no simple answers.
the prospects of civic participation in poor neighbourhoods are enhanced when there is a combination of high levels of civic engagement and a participatory approach to urban governance.
civic culture and citizen participation are interdependent, but not necessarily in the way that has been assumed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more the local state can be seen to be responsive to the needs and concerns of the community, the greater the likelihood of citizen involvement and participation.

the prospects for citizen involvement in urban governance are enhanced where the political culture is supportive of such involvement, where there are institutions that facilitate citizen involvement, and where the public policies adopted by the local authority are designed to promote participation.
civic culture and community can be enhanced by the right policy interventions and institutional structures, but the latter are more effective when the former is already present.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the creation of opportunities for citizen participation is likely to be a more effective strategy than the attempt to change the civic culture.

the prospects for citizen involvement are not determined simply by levels of civic culture, but by the extent to which the institutional structures of local government are supportive of citizen engagement and participation.
the creation of opportunities for participation can have a transformative impact on the civic culture and the political efficacy of citizens.
